name: K3PTA 3.2.214 — the free desktop app
body:
### K3PTA 3.2.214 — the free desktop app

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no K3PTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client.

**macOS · Apple silicon and Intel · free**

#### Why this patch exists

No behaviour changed. What changed is that the installer, the tag it hangs on and the licence it declares are now the same thing — measured against GitHub and against the packaged app, not read out of the source.

Three gaps, all found on 16 November 2026:

- **The tag named a different commit than the build.** `app-3.2.213` pointed at `064671a` (13 Nov, "Update README.md") while the shipped `.dmg` files were built from `3ca25a4` (15 Nov) — 1934 files apart, 133 of them delivered app code (`electron.js`, `package-lock.json`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/*`). Both commits are public and both are ancestors of `main`, but they share no common ancestor: the tag sat on the engine lineage, the build on the app lineage. `git checkout app-3.2.213` therefore handed an auditor tree `0d31a27d` while the binary was built from `a938a5f5`. **This release is built from the commit its own tag names: `7f18bef`.** The build writes that commit to `release/BAU-COMMIT.txt`, and step 5 of the proof chain compares it against the tag on GitHub.
- **The delivered package declared the wrong licence.** The `app.asar` inside `app-3.2.213` said `"license": "UNLICENSED"` while the download page said BUSL-1.1: the licence switch landed 34 minutes after that build, and `package-lock.json` kept `UNLICENSED` altogether. `tests/version.test.ts` now pins the licence in four places — `package.json`, `package-lock.json` `packages[""]`, `npm/package.json`, first line of `LICENSE` — the way it already pinned the version. Read out of both new packages: `version=3.2.214`, `license=BUSL-1.1`, `Info.plist=3.2.214`, `LICENSE="Business Source License 1.1"`.
- **The security notes described a release that does not exist.** `SECURITY-ENTERPRISE.md` called the desktop application proprietary while `LICENSE` names it as Licensed Work under BUSL-1.1, and described DMGs plus zips plus `latest-mac.yml` with SHA-512 digests. The published release carries three assets — two `.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` with SHA-256. Both sentences now state the measured shape. The app has no auto-updater, so zips, blockmaps and `latest-mac.yml` are built and stay on the build machine.

#### Verified before publishing, not after

`node scripts/release-beweisen.mjs 3.2.214` — exit 0, every step:

- both architectures carry `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 149` against the packaged Electron 44.4.1;
- both `.dmg` were mounted and the app inside them was launched in a throwaway home folder with a fresh 64-character key: the server answered, named `3.2.214`, encryption on;
- both surface markers are present in both bundles;
- **both packages name the same 6312 files and differ in content only in the two native binaries**;
- every checksum in `SHA256SUMS.txt` matches the file on disk.

The last of those is a new step, and it earned its place immediately: the first 3.2.214 build carried the build script's own Node-ABI backup (`better_sqlite3.node.vor-bau`) inside the arm64 `app.asar` — 6313 files against 6312 — while both packages started and reported the same version. The chain also refused an earlier build whose packaged SQLite module was a Node build (ABI 147), so the app opened a window whose server never listened. Nothing was published from either.

Source gates on the tagged commit: `npm run lint` 0 errors, 371 test files / 3913 tests green.

**Check it yourself:** `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached, one line per installer. After downloading both, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` must read `OK` on every line.

#### Note for macOS

This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarised (no Apple Developer ID): on first launch macOS says the developer cannot be verified. Apple removed right-click *Open* in macOS 15, so use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/K3PTA.app`. Once, then never again.

Nothing leaves your machine on its own: no account, no telemetry, no phone-home, no key check of any kind, and no auto-updater that would call a server. Chat only talks to a model provider you configure yourself, and the default is `localhost:11434` (Ollama).
